messages:
refactor: share the pointer internals between the toolkit's modules

JSON Patch needs more of RFC 6901 than resolvePointer gives: a pointer's
reference tokens, a walk along tokens already parsed, the way back from
tokens to a pointer, and the array-index rule.

Export those four from json-pointer.ts for the toolkit's own use, write
resolvePointer on top of the first two, and move the two questions every
module asks of a value — is it an object, how is its kind named in a
message — to json-value.ts. Behaviour is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: change JSON documents with standard patches (RFC 6902)

applyPatch(document, patch) applies a JSON Patch — add, remove, replace,
move, copy and test — and returns the result. The document handed in is
copied first, so it is never touched and a patch that fails halfway
through leaves it as it was; the values the patch carries are copied out
of it too, so a document and the patch that produced it share nothing.

The whole patch is checked before any of it is applied, and the failures
a caller tells apart get a class each: InvalidPatchError for a patch no
document could satisfy, PatchOperationError for an operation this
document defeats, TestFailedError for the precondition a test states.

Locations are read as resolvePointer reads them — own members only, no
path created along the way — with "-" given the append meaning RFC 6902
asks for. Member names go through Object.defineProperty, so "__proto__"
is a member of a document and never the prototype of one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
